messages:
Jules: Quick thread — finished a small bring-up + econ sweep for a 7B open model across two regions (us-west1, eu-west1) and two GPU families (A100-40GB, H100-80GB). Posting highlights so we can decide defaults for onboarding and Dedicated sizing.

BenchBot: Raw CSV uploaded -> gs://redwood-bench/1965432199/noprefix7b_sweep.csv and summary pushed to perf dash https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/1965432199 :white_check_mark:

Marco: TL;DR numbers (median across 200 runs, warm KV cache where noted):
```
- us-west1 / A100-40GB (batch=8, prefill=512, decode=128, q=fp16): prefill median 42ms, decode median 8.5ms/token, tokens/sec ~520, est $/1M tokens = $28
- us-west1 / H100-80GB (batch=8, prefill=512, decode=128, q=fp16, flash-attn): prefill 31ms, decode 6.2ms/token, tokens/sec ~720, est $/1M tokens = $22
- eu-west1 / A100: +7–9% latency vs us-west1 (infra noise), tokens/sec ~480, $/1M ≈ $30
- eu-west1 / H100: similar +8% latency vs us-west, tokens/sec ~660, $/1M ≈ $24
Notes: prefill dominated by kv-cache copy for longer prefills; H100 wins more on decode than prefill.
```

Priya: Nice. Which kernel builds were used for each? and what quantization variants did you try?

Marco: We used the following: A100 -> cuBLAS + fused gemm kernels (runtime v1.6); H100 -> flash-attn v2 + optimized fwd kernels (runtime v1.9). Quantization sweep: fp16, q4_0, q4_1. q4_0 gave ~1.8x tokens/sec vs fp16 but had a small quality hit.

Kamil: fwiw, past batch 16 A100 throughput flattens due to SM contention; H100 scales to batch 32 nicely for decode heavy workloads. Also saw different kernel memory-pressure behaviors when seq_prefill > 1024.

Marco: Command we used for reproducibility:
```
./run_infer.sh --model noprefix-7b --gpu a100,h100 --region us-west1,eu-west1 --batch 8 --prefill 512 --decode 128 --quant fp16,q4_0,q4_1 --runs 200
```

Jules: Can you paste the exact tokens/sec -> $/1M calc? I want the economics line for the runbook.

Marco: Sure — formula: cost_per_hour_gpu * (3600 / (tokens_per_second * avg_tokens_per_request)) * 1e6. We used $3.0/hr for A100-40GB reserved price and $4.0/hr for H100-80GB (on our Dedicated pricing sheet). Example: H100 720 tps * 32 avg tokens/request -> 720*32 = 23040 tokens/sec -> 82.9M tokens/hour -> $4 / 82.9M * 1M ≈ $48/hour per 1M? (oops that's confusing in-plain) Simplified: per-million = (gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_hour) * 1e6. With numbers above per-million ≈ $22 for H100, $28 for A100 (matches the table).

Priya: Thanks. Did you evaluate q4_0 quality? what's the regression?

Marco: Quick eval (held-out prompt set, n=1200): q4_0 reduces generation latency 1.8x but drops our primary metric (ROUGE-like score) by 0.9 points absolute and increases hallucination flags by ~2%. q4_1 is a good middle ground: ~1.4x perf gain, <0.3pt metric delta.

Kamil: Important: for latency-SLOs under 50ms per-turn, H100 + q4_1 is the sweet spot for small bursty workloads; for steady high-throughput A100 reserved capacity still gives better $/token when you use aggressive batching and caching.

Jules: Regional effects — anything surprising?

Marco: eu-west1 had slightly worse tail latencies due to lower instance density (more noisy neighbors) and slightly older NIC firmware on some nodes. Multi-AZ crosszone routing added 2–6ms in 95p for prefill in one of our runs. Not a showstopper but worth noting for strict latency SLAs.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INF-3287 "eu-west1 noisy-nodes affecting infer tail latencies" (auto-tagged eng-infra) :spiral_calendar:

Priya: For onboarding doc: propose default profiles: 1) dev/smoke -> A100 fp16 small batch, 2) burst-latency -> H100 q4_1, 3) cost-optimized steady -> A100 q4_1 with aggressive batching & prefix cache. I'll draft and link.

Jules: Action items:
- Marco: open a perf ticket to add H100/q4_1 as a recommended variant in model-onboarding (assign to you)
- Kamil: can you sweep batch scaling up to 64 on H100 and paste results in the CSV?
- Priya: add these rows to the onboarding runbook and call out quality thresholds for q4_0/q4_1

Marco: Will do. I'll also add kernel tags (flash-attn vs cublas) to each perf row so we can filter dash by kernel.

Priya: Thanks — useful snapshot. If we agree, I'll use these as the default perf gates for new 7B model brings. :thumbsup:

Jules: Agree. Nice quick sweep, saves us time picking defaults.

BenchBot: Summary card created on perf dash + exported pngs -> https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/1965432199/summary.png :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Marco: I'll follow up with a short note on observed kernel-level memory artifacts (LLM runtime issue #412)."
